descriptors.concept_name: Split accounting for compound financial instruments
descriptors.definition: Split accounting allocates the initial carrying amount of a compound financial instrument between its liability and equity components without generating any initial gain or loss. The liability component is determined by discounting its cash flows at a market rate for a similar non-convertible liability, while the equity component is assigned the residual amount.
inclusion: Instruments containing both liability and equity components
exclusion: Simple financial instruments with only liability or equity features
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from single-category instruments by separately measuring debt obligations and residual equity stakes on initial recognition rather than classifying the entire instrument under one category.

descriptors.definition: Non-equity embedded derivative features, such as an issuer's call option contained within a compound financial instrument, are categorized and included as part of the liability component. The residual value after deducting the combined liability and derivative obligations is then allocated to the equity component.
inclusion: Early redemption features in convertible instruments
exclusion: Equity conversion options meeting equity classification criteria
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from standard equity conversion options because non-equity derivatives like issuer call options are grouped with the liability component rather than assigned to equity.

descriptors.concept_name: Conversion or early settlement of compound financial instruments
descriptors.definition: Conversion at maturity involves derecognizing the liability component and transferring it directly to equity without generating a gain or loss. Early settlement requires allocating consideration paid based on current fair values of the remaining liability and equity components, recognizing any resulting gain or loss for the liability portion.
inclusion: Conversion of convertible instruments at maturity
Early repurchase or redemption before maturity
exclusion: Initial recognition and allocation of compound instruments
Standard subsequent measurement of pure financial liabilities
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from maturity conversion by early settlement requiring the immediate allocation of repurchase consideration and recognition of associated liability gains or losses.

descriptors.definition: When an entity reacquires its own equity instruments, the consideration paid is deducted directly from equity without recognizing any gain or loss in profit or loss. Such treasury shares are never recognized as financial assets regardless of the acquisition motive.
inclusion: Entity's own equity instruments reacquired and held
Treasury shares held by consolidated group members
exclusion: Shares held purely in a fiduciary agency capacity on behalf of external clients
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from financial assets because an entity's own equity instruments can never be recognized as financial assets upon reacquisition.

descriptors.definition: The classification of a financial instrument dictates whether related returns and value changes flow through profit or loss or directly into equity. Specifically, liabilities generate expenses or income in profit or loss, whereas equity distributions are recognized directly in equity.
inclusion: Interest and dividends on financial liabilities
Incremental transaction costs of equity and compound transactions
exclusion: Fair value changes of an entity's own equity instruments
Abandoned equity transaction costs recognized as expense
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished by instrument classification, routing liability-related returns through profit or loss while recording equity distributions directly through equity reserves.

descriptors.concept_name: OFFSETTING A FINANCIAL ASSET AND A FINANCIAL LIABILITY
descriptors.definition: Financial assets and liabilities are offset to present a net amount in the balance sheet only when an entity has a currently enforceable legal right of set-off and intends either to settle on a net basis or realize and settle simultaneously. This offsetting treatment is distinct from derecognition and does not inherently generate a gain or loss.
inclusion: Net presentation of recognized financial assets and liabilities under strict enforceability and settlement intent criteria
Three-party agreements establishing valid debtor set-off rights
exclusion: Separate financial instruments merely emulating net outcomes without legal set-off rights
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from derecognition because offsetting retains both gross items on or off the books via net presentation without generating gains or losses, whereas derecognition removes items and can trigger profit or loss recognition.
